newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa may see near 3 pct growth in 1997 - Stals.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa may see near 3 pct growth in 1997 - Stals.

text.p: South Africa's economy could grow by close to three percent in 1997, little changed from the 3.1 percent recorded in 1997, Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said on Tuesday.
"It is quite possible that the growth rate of the gross domestic production can be maintained at a level not very far below three percent for this year," he said in an interview.
Stals said most economists at the start of the year, including those from the Reserve Bank, had been looking for a slowdown in real GDP in 1997 to around 2.0 to 2.5 percent.
But recent data from the fourth quarter of 1996 and the early months of 1997 suggested the economy was performing more strongly that expected, boosted by exports.

"It is not impossible that the motivation of the export industries because of the devaluation of last year can boost the growth rate in the economy and maybe the total real economic production of 1997 will not be much below the performances of the last two years," Stals said.
